stem: A liquid of density $\rho$ is coming out of a hose pipe of radius $a$ with horizontal speed $v$ and hits a mesh. 50% of the liquid passes through the mesh unaffected. 25% loses all of its momentum and 25% comes back with the same speed. The resultant pressure on the mesh will be :
solution:
Momentum per second carried by the liquid is $\rho av^2$ (per unit area $\rho v^2$).

Force due to reflected liquid $= 2\times\frac14\rho av^2$; due to stopped liquid $= \frac14\rho av^2$.

Total force $= \frac34\rho av^2$, net pressure $= \frac34\rho v^2$

stem: The energy required to ionise a hydrogen like ion in its ground state is 9 Rydbergs. What is the wavelength of the radiation emitted when the electron in this ion jumps from the second excited state to the ground state?
solution:
Ionisation energy $= 13.6Z^2$ eV $= 9\times13.6$ eV $\Rightarrow Z = 3$

$\dfrac1\lambda = RZ^2\left(\dfrac{1}{1^2} - \dfrac{1}{3^2}\right) = 1.09\times10^7\times9\times\dfrac89 \Rightarrow \lambda = 11.4$ nm

stem: Following figure shows two processes $A$ and $B$ for a gas. If $\Delta Q_A$ and $\Delta Q_B$ are the amount of heat absorbed by the system in two cases, $\Delta U_A$ and $\Delta U_B$ are changes in internal energies, respectively, then:
solution: Initial and final states are the same for both processes, so $\Delta U_A = \Delta U_B$. Work done in process A is greater (larger area). By the first law, $\Delta Q = \Delta U + W \Rightarrow \Delta Q_A > \Delta Q_B$

stem: A substance $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ yields on oxidation a compound, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$ which gives an oxime and a positive iodoform test. The original substance on treatment with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$. The structure of the compound is

$$\text{D-(+)-Glyceraldehyde} \xrightarrow[\text{(ii) H}_2\text{O/H}^+,\ \text{(iii) HNO}_3]{\text{(i) HCN}}$$

The products formed in the above reaction are:
options: One optically active and one meso product
One optically inactive and one meso product
solution: HCN addition gives two diastereomeric cyanohydrins; hydrolysis and $\text{HNO}_3$ oxidation give two tartaric acids: one meso (optically inactive) and one optically active.
